blocker: DF cr5o_scope_uml_backslash_start: '\startuml' / '!theme cr5obg from .' / 'Pukeko -> Takahe : bsl' / '\enduml'. Java renders it; 32684f81e renders it; the tip reports 'no registered sequence command accepts "\startuml"'. Inherited from the sprite/participant line (strict sequence admission); d28dd64a9, 9ed52f435 and 9dc1af5f9 fail the same way.

java_trace.pipe: Pipe#readSingleDiagram (Pipe.java:180-225) tests line.startsWith("@start"), case-sensitive, with no leading whitespace. A '\startuml' input finds no start mark, so Pipe returns "@startuml\n" + input + "@enduml\n" (line 217).
java_trace.block_builder: BlockUmlBuilder#<init> (BlockUmlBuilder.java:100-133) reads the Preprocessor (ReadFilterMergeLines) lines. Every line for which StartUtils#isStartDirective holds restarts the block (current = new ArrayList, line 101-104); the first StartUtils#isEndDirective line closes it (line 126-133); an end with no open block is ignored. So for the wrapped '\startuml' input the block is '\startuml' .. '\enduml', and Pipe's '@startuml'/'@enduml' lie outside it.
java_trace.start_directive: StartUtils#isStartDirective (StartUtils.java:52-54) is DiagramType#findStartTypes(s).size() > 0. findStartTypes (core/DiagramType.java:69-92) skips Character#isWhitespace, requires '@' or '\\', then check("start") and at least one more character; getTypes (line 94+) switches on Character.toLowerCase of the next character and check(key) for the type. check (line 218-220) is regionMatches(true, ...): both 'start' and the type are case-insensitive. An unrecognised type is EnumSet.of(UNKNOWN), still non-empty, so still a start directive.
java_trace.end_directive: StartUtils#isEndDirective (StartUtils.java:110-112, via startsWithDirectiveKeyword at 86-108) skips Character#isWhitespace, requires '@' or '\\' and regionMatches(start, "end") case-sensitively. Rust already ports this (is_end_directive, round 4).
java_trace.type: PSystemBuilder#createPSystem (PSystemBuilder.java:210-212) reads findStartTypes(source.get(0)): '\startuml' gives SEQUENCE (case 'u', check("uml")), so checkEndingBackslash is set and the UML factories run.
java_trace.case: '@STARTUML' .. '@ENDUML' (DF cr5o_scope_uml_upper_start, a Java Syntax Error): Pipe finds no '@start' and wraps; '@STARTUML' IS a start directive (case-insensitive) and opens the block; '@ENDUML' is NOT an end directive (case-sensitive 'end'), so it is a content line and the UML factories reject it; Pipe's '@enduml' closes the block. Java's rejection comes from the end test, not from a case-sensitive start test.

rust_divergence: Three Rust main-path sites recognise only a literal '@start': PreprocessContext#execute_one_line's block-start test (trimmed.starts_with("@start")), parse::split_blocks (strip_prefix("@start") and starts_with("@end")), and parse::detect_type (strip_prefix("@start")). A '\startuml' line is therefore no block start: the preprocessor emits it as a Plain line and the sequence parser rejects it.
planned_change: preprocess: the block-start test at include depth 0 becomes StartUtils#isStartDirective on the merged line (start_directive_type(line).is_some()), so '\start<type>' opens the block exactly as '@start<type>' does; the EBNF flag uses start_type_is(kind, "ebnf"). The first-start-only rule, the later-start handling and Pipe's literal '@start' test are unchanged, so nested and later starts behave for '\' as they already do for '@'.

parse::split_blocks: start = start_directive_type, end = is_end_directive (both exported pub(crate) from preprocess), so a '\start' block is split like an '@start' block and closes at its first Java end directive.

parse::detect_type: the type word comes from start_directive_type, lower-cased (getTypes switches on Character.toLowerCase and check is case-insensitive). '@STARTUML' therefore types as uml; its '@ENDUML' stays a content line (is_end_directive is case-sensitive), so it stays rejected as in Java.

Unit tests: '\startuml' .. '\enduml' parses as a sequence diagram; '\startmindmap' .. '\endmindmap' as a mindmap; split_blocks splits '\start'/'\end' blocks; '@STARTUML' .. '@ENDUML' is still an error.
not_changed: Pipe#readSingleDiagram's literal '@start' test; nested-start semantics (BlockUmlBuilder restarts the block, Rust keeps the first start); start tests inside includes; every parser's own start/end skipping. Out of scope per the parent: EBNF short-comment exemption, theme-line positions for non-UML parsers, JSON/YAML themes, theme backgrounds in timing/mindmap/wbs, wbs/gantt/nwdiag/mindmap false accepts, the clippy dead code, YAML after a leading comment.
